---
title: "Components and native callouts"
---

## Callout mapping

The extension maps native Quarto types to a fixed visual meaning: note is muted
blue with info, tip is teal with flame, important is lavender with circle alert,
warning is amber with triangle alert, and caution is coral with octagon alert.
The icons are bundled local Lucide SVGs, exposed as CSS masks rather than a new
runtime.

The shell, title, semantic alpha border/fill, 5px radius, icon, and native
chevron follow Quartz's callout showcase as closely as Quarto's DOM permits.
Quarto's five native types, their collapse behavior, and nested callouts are
the current interface. Quartz's additional family aliases are intentionally not
invented here: exposing them needs a separate authoring syntax transformer and
public contract rather than a brittle visual-only imitation.

::: {.callout-note title="Note / 註記"}
Use note for context that informs but does not interrupt the main thread.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Tip / 提示"}
Use tip for a helpful practice. The icon remains the flame at all depths.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Important / 重要"}
Use important for a material reader decision.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Warning / 警告"}
Use warning when readers should inspect a condition before proceeding.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="Caution / 注意"}
Use caution for a concrete risk whose consequence should remain visible.
:::

## Native edge cases

::: {.callout-note title="A deliberately long custom native title that wraps naturally on a compact phone without changing the callout type"}
Long custom titles remain part of the native header.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="" icon=false appearance="simple"}
This is a native titleless, iconless simple tip. It is still semantically a tip.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Collapsed native warning" collapse="true"}
This body is available through Quarto's own disclosure control; QDK does not
replace its behavior.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="Expanded native caution" collapse="false" appearance="minimal"}
Minimal appearance continues to be Quarto's presentation choice, with Kit
colors applied to the supported callout DOM.
:::

## Native thematic break

QDK deliberately leaves headings unruled. Add a divider only when a reading
transition needs one, using ordinary Markdown rather than a Kit component.

---

Source authoring:

```markdown
## Native thematic break

---
```

## Tables, code, and equations

| Component | Local behavior | Reader concern |
|---|---|---|
| Table / 表格 | A wide table scrolls inside its own responsive wrapper instead of assigning arbitrary cell widths. | Keep headers meaningful. |
| Code / 程式碼 | Indentation and Quarto copy controls remain native; long lines scroll locally. | Do not turn source into prose. |
| Formula / 公式 | Display mathematics may scroll locally on narrow screens. | Preserve symbols and reading order. |

```python
def describe_reading_surface(theme: str, width: int) -> str:
    return f"{theme} surface at {width}px retains local overflow boundaries"

long_line = "qdk keeps this intentionally long source line in a local preformatted scroll area rather than allowing it to widen the whole page beyond the reader viewport"
print(describe_reading_surface("dark", 360), long_line)
```

For a deliberately long expression, the local math container protects the page
width while leaving the equation legible:

$$
\mathcal{R}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{\alpha_k\,\exp\left(-\frac{(x-\mu_k)^2}{2\sigma_k^2}\right)}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma_k} + \int_0^\infty \frac{\lambda^2 + \omega^2 + \eta^2}{(\lambda + \omega + \eta)^2}\,d\omega.
$$

The [saved notebook output](notebook-output.qmd) is a separate, real simple
execution artifact rather than a simulated output block.
